cause_quote: It replaced the uncancellable spawnSync probe with `await runUtf8CommandWithTimeout(..., { ..., signal: params?.signal, killProcessTree: true })`, so a cancelled caller now SIGTERM/SIGKILLs `claude auth status` mid-refresh.
user_saw: After model discovery was cancelled during a Claude login refresh, the next Claude CLI turn stalled about 10 seconds or failed with 'another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh'.
summary: The Claude CLI auth-status probe no longer passes the caller's abort signal to the child process; a cancelled caller waits for the probe to exit on its own and only the 10 s deadline terminates it.
reasoning: The removed `signal: params?.signal` line was added by 2640154bcf80 (#137071), whose diff converts probeClaudeCliAuthStatus from a blocking spawnSync (which callers could not cancel and whose timeout only sent a SIGTERM that Claude Code defers) to the async runner with the caller's signal and process-tree kill (SIGTERM then SIGKILL 300 ms later). That makes a cancelled discovery kill the refresh and orphan .oauth_refresh.lock; before it, a cancelled caller could not kill the probe. Medium because I could not confirm that the Claude Code version current in September 2026 already refreshed tokens under the lock inside `auth status`; if that came later the case would be latent.
